myths.title: Primary Attestation
myths.text: Avalokiteśvara is attested in the canonical Buddhist sources as a figure associated with compassion, mercy, bodhisattva.

myths.title: Name and Meaning
myths.text: The name means "Lord who looks down in compassion" and reflects the figure's role in the tradition.

lore.syncretism: Avalokiteśvara appears within the Buddhist tradition and has influenced later retellings, artistic depictions, and scholarly study. The Unicode restoration preserves the name's distinctive orthography for contemporary use.
lore.culturalLegacy: Avalokiteśvara continues to appear in scholarship, art, and popular reception as a significant figure of the Buddhist tradition. Restoring the name in Unicode returns the original marks that ASCII removes.
lore.extendedMeditation: Avalokiteśvara embodies compassion, mercy, bodhisattva in the Buddhist imagination. The name's restoration is not merely cosmetic: it recovers the stress, length, and script that make the figure recognizable in the source tradition.
lore.archaeology: Avalokiteśvara is attested in the textual and iconographic record of the Buddhist tradition.
